name: Hilda Sharp
highlight: From Cap Gris-Nez to the cliffs below Dover in 14 hours 58 minutes, August 1928.
biography: Hilda Winifred Sharp, known as Laddie, lived in Hither Green in south-east London. She trained at Brighton with Jabez Wolffe, who had made repeated attempts on the Channel himself. Sharp succeeded on her first attempt at the age of 18.

In August 1928 Sharp swam from Cap Gris-Nez to Lydden Spout on the English coast. She used the trudgen stroke. William Burgess and Joe Costa accompanied her on the Alsace, and Wolffe was aboard as her trainer. Her recorded crossing time was 14 hours 58 minutes.

The dated swim log records a 00:50 departure and a 15:48 finish on Friday 24 August 1928. The archive’s introduction gives 28 August and a 16:48 finish. The dated entry is the one whose clocks agree with the registered duration. Neither entry gives a time zone.

lines.label: Historical discrepancy
lines.text: The archive’s biographical introduction instead gives 28 August and a 16:48 finish. The dated swim entry agrees with the registered elapsed time. The precise clock readings remain qualified.

lines.text: William Burgess and Joe Costa, aboard Alsace. The archive also names Costa as timekeeper.

lines.label: Recognition
lines.text: The crossing appears in the CSA register. The detailed historical entry classifies it as independent.
How the record was checked
CSA individual record 2242
CS&PF historical database, swim 442816
Channel Swimming Dover, dated swim entry and biographical introduction
Dover.UK historical swim record

The two registers agree on year, direction and duration. The historical database attributes recognition to the CSA and gives no clocks. The dated archive entry and Dover.UK agree on 24 August. The archive spells the landing “Lyddon Spout” in the swim entry and “Lydden Spout” in its introduction.
